tone.target: jangly British breakup with light swirl
tone.profile: jangly British breakup with light swirl
tone.summary: A bright, chimey signal chain utilizing a classic UK amp model (AC30 TB) paired with chorus and room reverb to achieve the desired jangly, breakup sound reminiscent of Vox AC30 tones.

rig.name: Traffic - Dear Mr. Fantasy - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide subtle grit and boost the upper mids for breakup character.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to emulate a light, slightly broken-up tube preamp tone rather than a pure clean booster.

alternatives.reason: A general boost could work but lacks the specific tonal character of the Green OD.

blocks.purpose: Keep the signal clean and focused on natural breakup tones.
blocks.gap: No dedicated distortion unit is needed; the Green OD provides sufficient grit.

blocks.purpose: Keep the tone open and focused on natural guitar tones.
blocks.gap: No wah effect is required for this specific jangly sound.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the bright, chimey sound of a Vox AC30.
Provide a classic British cabinet voicing that complements the AC30 tone.
blocks.gap: While the source suggests 1x12 or 2x12, the UK Vintage 4x12 is chosen for its overall bright and articulate character which suits the jangly sound.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative if a more American/Fender-esque voicing was desired.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the upper mids and brightness while controlling low-end muddiness.
Add the required subtle 'swirl' or vibrato effect.
Provide the required short spring room ambience without sounding too wet.
blocks.gap: The 'Room' reverb is used as a general space effect, fulfilling the requirement for a subtle ambient tail.

alternatives.reason: A Plate could also provide room ambience but might sound too metallic.

blocks.purpose: Avoid big delay as per the 'avoid' list.
blocks.gap: The effect is bypassed to ensure no noticeable delay artifacts.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by switching from a 4x12 to a smaller, more period-appropriate British voicing (1x12 or 2x12) to better match the jangly Vox AC30 tone.

proposals.reason: Better matches the single-speaker, chimey nature of the AC30 and source era.
proposals.whenToUse: After initial testing with current preset
